segment: Other labor-scarce or paperwork-heavy Alaska SMBs

candidates.location: Anchorage HQ (12050 Industry Way, Ste O-1, Anchorage, AK 99515), with offices in Seward, Juneau, and Tacoma WA. Serves Western/Central/Southeast Alaska, Bristol Bay, Kuskokwim, Norton Sound, Kotzebue Sound, Arctic.
candidates.what_they_do: Scheduled marine barge freight from Seattle/Tacoma/Seward to Alaska ports and villages, plus charter and project cargo. Owns its own tugs, barges, landing craft, cranes, forklifts and container fleet. Running a published six-voyage 2026 program (26-01 through 26-06) serving Juneau, Seward, Naknek, Dillingham, Bethel, Nome, Kotzebue and numerous village stops.

structural_pain.primary_quote: All shipments are personally quoted by a project manager, who will answer all questions and walk you through all the steps needed from booking to delivery, to receiving.
structural_pain.why_structural: Every single shipment is quoted and shepherded by a human project manager end to end. That is a published, self-described manual intake and quoting process running against a fixed six-voyage window and cargo cutoffs, not a website defect.
structural_pain.supporting_quote_1: Departure from Seattle, Tacoma, and Seward typically occurs 3-5 days after cargo cutoff
structural_pain.supporting_quote_3: It got very cold the day we got there. It got down to, like, single digits and ice came out of the mountains, and rivers, and sloughs everywhere.
structural_pain.supporting_quote_3_note: Attributed by KYUK to General Manager Allyn Long. KYUK also reports Long saying the company should consider ending its barge season earlier. That second line is the reporter's rendering, treat it as reported speech, not a verbatim company statement.
structural_pain.seasonal_relevance: Freeze-up scheduling on the Kuskokwim and Norton Sound is decided in late August. Their own published season and their GM's own on-record freeze-up experience sit exactly on the 2026-08-10 seasonal angle.

decision_maker_evidence.named_person: Allyn Long, owner and General Manager
decision_maker_evidence.quote: Alaska Logistics is owned and managed by General Manager Allyn Long... After ten years as the Logistics Manager at Osborne Construction Co., which is a major general contractor for many Alaska Projects; Allyn had the experience and knowledge to start up Alaska Logistics.
decision_maker_evidence.published_email: none. No email address appears on any fetched page. Published phones only: (907) 416-2435 office, (866) 585-3281 toll free, plus after-hours (206) 799-1840 and (907) 545-6907. Contact form on alaskalogistics.net. Do not pattern-invent an address.

candidates.reputation_screen: FLAG, not disqualifying, but the room must know it. KYUK (public radio, Bethel) reported in November 2021 that Alaska Logistics left two barges frozen in the Kuskokwim River after an early freeze-up, that the US Coast Guard was investigating both incidents and the company could face fines for obstructing waterways, and that Lower Yukon School District teacher housing construction in Scammon Bay was delayed. A separate KYUK piece from May 2020 covers an unattended Alaska Logistics barge floating down the Kuskokwim. No fraud, False Claims Act, immigration enforcement contracting, or labor litigation found in a light screen. Any outreach must not lecture them about this and must not pretend it did not happen.
candidates.confidence: High that the company is real, Alaska-operating, and currently running a 2026 voyage program (verified on the live .net site). MEDIUM on the employee count of about fifty and the April-through-October season, both of which come from the legacy alaska-logistics.com about page that survives while contact.html now 301s to alaskalogistics.net. KYUK's 2021 reporting says deliveries typically ran into mid-November, so the season line and the reporting disagree. Re-verify season and headcount before any of it goes in a study.

candidates.what_they_do: Combined architecture, engineering and surveying firm. Land surveying services include as-builts and mortgage surveys, boundary surveys, plot plans, topographic surveys, building stakes, and platting and subdividing, coordinated across Municipality of Anchorage, Mat-Su Borough, State of Alaska and Federal platting authorities.

structural_pain.primary_quote: extensive experience performing subdivisions throughout the state
structural_pain.why_structural: Their published platting workflow runs the same submittal through four different classes of authority, municipal (Anchorage), borough (Mat-Su), State and Federal, each with its own code and its own preliminary-plat review cycle, then final recording with State of Alaska Recording Districts. A multi-jurisdiction submittal treadmill is a structural operating load, and it is exactly what stacks up now as the construction season closes.

structural_pain.seasonal_relevance: Field season closes in roughly six weeks, so as-builts, elevation work and plat submittals for this season's projects are queueing now.

candidates.what_they_do: Environmental engineering and industrial hygiene consultancy, founded 1979. structural_pain.why_structural: A three-office firm carrying two standing open technical roles, Environmental Engineer-in-Training (Fairbanks) and Certified Industrial Hygienist (Fairbanks or Anchorage), is publishing that it cannot staff to its workload. A Certified Industrial Hygienist is one of the hardest credentials to hire in Alaska. That is labor scarcity as published fact, not a website defect. The underlying business is entirely deliverable-and-report driven, five disciplines every one of which ends in a regulatory report.
structural_pain.supporting_quote_1: His role encompasses hazardous materials assessments, environmental investigations, contaminated site remediation, Phase I and Phase II ESAs, indoor air quality assessments, and design work for demolition and decommissioning projects.

structural_pain.seasonal_relevance: Field-season closeout means the Phase I/Phase II and site characterization reports written from this summer's fieldwork all come due in the same weeks.
